title: The monadic small-model bound can be zero despite requiring nonempty models.
details: Logicalslide6 (finaloverlay expandedPDFpage64) states that a satisfiable formula with k predicates, m constants and ℓ quantifiers has a model with at most(m+ℓ)2^k elements, without a positivity condition. For the sentence⊤ in the empty predicate language, m=ℓ=k=0, so the stated bound is0 although a nonempty model needs at least1element. The reservoir argument is repaired by a positive cap; the corpus treats sentences without constants and proves max(1,q)2^k, where q counts primitive quantifiers. No upstream correction is inferred.
